title: Coding without the web
description: Small, practical guides for building and debugging offline.

cards.title: Debug one failure at a time
cards.summary: Make the failure repeatable, reduce it to the smallest input, inspect the actual error, and change one thing at a time.
steps: Write down the exact action, input, error, and expected result.
Reproduce it with the smallest example you can make.
Add a log or breakpoint at the boundary where the result first becomes wrong.
Change one cause, rerun, and keep a regression check.

cards.title: Save work with Git
cards.summary: Git records versions locally, even without internet. Check changes before committing and keep commits focused.
steps: Run git status to see changed files.
Run git diff to inspect what changed.
Stage intended files with git add, then commit with a clear message.
Before trying a risky edit, commit a working checkpoint.

cards.title: Start a small Python script
cards.summary: Write a function for one task, call it with a known input, and print or test the result before expanding it.
steps: Create a .py file and define a function with a clear name.
Use a tiny known input to check the output.
Handle expected errors explicitly rather than hiding every exception.
Keep useful examples as repeatable tests.
